articles.title: UFO files: 'Black triangles' moving at extraordinary speed spotted over sensitive US site
articles.summary: Two senior military observers have reported seeing a mysterious black triangular object travelling at an estimated 1,800mph over a sensitive site in the
articles.body: Two senior military observers have reported seeing a mysterious black triangular object travelling at an estimated 1,800mph over a sensitive site in the western United States earlier this year, according to a report released by the Trump administration on Friday.The observers described the unidentified object as unlike any conventional military aircraft. According to their account submitted to the defence department, it disappeared suddenly and silently within seconds, without leaving an exhaust trail or any other visible evidence, the Guardian reported.The object was said to resemble a delta-wing drone, with an estimated wingspan of between nine and 15 feet (2.75 to 4.5 metres). The report classified it as an “unidentified anomalous phenomenon” (UAP), the term increasingly used by military and government agencies instead of UFO.The location of the alleged sighting has been redacted in the report. The observers were described as having “extensive operational experience working alongside government agencies”.However, the document offers limited visual evidence to support the account. It contains nine identical images of a canyon, with small triangular silhouettes superimposed on the landscape to illustrate the object's reported movement.Pentagon's UFO disclosuresThe latest release is part of a series of documents made public by the Pentagon since May, following US President Donald Trump's pledge to disclose previously classified information about UFO sightings and the government's knowledge of potential extraterrestrial life.Trump ordered a broader disclosure in February, following years of public scrutiny and allegations of a government cover-up.In 2023, a former intelligence official told Congress that successive administrations had concealed information about UFOs and that the government possessed crashed alien spacecraft. Those allegations have not established that extraterrestrial craft exist.The pace of disclosures has slowed in recent months, with Friday's release containing fewer than 25 text documents and no videos or photographs. While several earlier reports included photographs or footage of alleged sightings, the black-triangle account relies on observers' descriptions and illustrative images.The report does not establish the object's identity or provide independent evidence confirming the observers' account.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2010, while tracing Trosley’s history with Google Earth, Kent volunteers followed crop marks to a Roman villa; excavation revealed a bathhouse, painted walls and underfloor heating
articles.summary: A community excavation led by Kent Archaeological Society volunteers uncovered a high-status Roman villa near Trosley, revealing a rare bathhouse, painted walls, and advanced heating systems, thanks to innovative crop mark detection through Google Earth.
articles.body: The Kent Archaeological Society runs the ongoing Trosley Heritage Project, which Current Archaeology describes as a larger landscape project studying how Trosley has been inhabited over time. Part of this work is done at the desk, with members searching publicly available satellite imagery of the fields for signs of buried features. Because crops can grow differently above buried walls and ditches, creating crop marks visible in satellite imagery even when they are not apparent at ground level, volunteers noticed a distinctive pattern in farmland near the village. Kent’s Historic Environment Record provides the relevant heritage record. The Society later held a community excavation of the site, with residents working alongside the Society’s more experienced excavators and the dig also hosted school visits. The dig uncovered partial foundations of what may have been a high-status Roman villa, along with painted wall plaster and remains of the villa’s hypocaust system.Crop marks in Google Earth images from 2007 and earlier finds of Roman building materialThe Kent Historic Environment Record entry titled Possible Romano-British building, Trottiscliffe describes a faint cropmark visible in Google Earth images from 2007 and in aerial photographs from 2008. It is described on record as two squares connected by a rectangle, around 28 metres in length but no wider than 14 metres. The same record notes that roof tiles, box flue tiles, fragments of painted plaster and coins dating from the 3rd and 4th centuries were found in a field north of Trottiscliffe and that fieldwalking there turned up Roman roofing tile and pottery together with mortared rubble suggesting a buried Roman masonry structure, perhaps a villa.The Society’s own report, Roman villa with bathhouse and hypocaust system revealed near Trosley, written by Jacob Scott, appeared in issue 119 (Winter 2022) of the Kent Archaeological Society magazine. It describes how crop markings were spotted on Google Earth after a particularly dry period, which led to fieldwalking and test pits in the year before the excavation. The cropmark projections created by Chris Blair-Myers were used for trench placement. Current Archaeology, as reported by The Past, says the Society first found the site in 2010 during a survey of Google Earth images, while the 2007 date given by the record and the Society refers to the date of the images that showed the cropmarks.The September 2022 community excavation and what trench 1 revealedIn excess of 50 volunteers assisted with the September 2022 excavation directed by site director Richard Taylor, according to The Past in its write-up of issue 394 of Current Archaeology. Trench 1, which was dug on the main building, revealed foundations of the villa made of local ragstone and flint. Third and fourth-century ceramics found at the site include local coarse wares, Oxfordshire wares and some Samian wares alongside several coins dating back to the 4th century.The Kent Archaeological Society magazine report also mentions a quantity of multicoloured painted wall plaster from Trench 1, which likely adorned the villa’s interior walls. Archaeology magazine lists a fourth-century copper-alloy strap-end shaped like an amphora, a small Romano-British key and two fourth-century coins. For many volunteers, it was a first excavation, Taylor told Artnet News and he pointed out that most archaeology in Kent is developer-led, which makes openings for volunteers uncommon. The same report says the Society first identified the villa complex from Google Earth images and that volunteers later helped excavate trenches over the main building and what is believed to be a bathhouse.A pilae stack at least 11 tiles high and a rare surviving hypocaustOther trenches discovered the foundations of a bathhouse and a pilae stack, which is an upright stack of tiles that supported the floor above the heating room. The Past describes how it had risen to at least 11 tiles, but the bottom tile remains to be excavated. At some time, possibly during the 4th century, the bath house seems to have been filled up and converted into another structure. The metalled surface of compacted flints was discovered west of the bath house structure. Taylor said in a statement, reported by Artnet News, that among the hundreds of villas across Kent, a surviving hypocaust is rare. Archaeology magazine includes his assertion that running the hypocaust was costly because it needed an uninterrupted supply of wood fuel and a labor force to run it.Farming wealth and the September 2023 return to Trosley CourtTaylor told Artnet News that the occupants probably farmed the surrounding land and sold their crops in London, Canterbury or Gaul. The Society’s magazine report said it planned to return in September 2023 to investigate the bathhouse further and the Society’s own later page on the site states that its 2023 excavations at Trosley Court revealed a Romano-British bathhouse.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Largest ever’: Elon Musk donates $443 million to Trump's campaign ahead of US midterms
articles.summary: Billionaire Elon Musk has spent more than $442 million on Republican campaigns and political groups ahead of the November 3 US midterm elections, emerging
articles.body: Billionaire Elon Musk has spent more than $442 million on Republican campaigns and political groups ahead of the November 3 US midterm elections, emerging as the largest individual political donor in US history.Federal Election Commission (FEC) filings show that Musk made three direct contributions totalling $74.8 million to his America PAC between October 6 and 14, Forbes reported. An additional $1.98 million came through his company, United States of America Inc., taking his total contributions for the first half of October to nearly $77 million.America PAC is a political action committee founded and heavily backed by Musk to support Republican and conservative candidates through voter turnout operations and digital campaigns.According to Forbes, America PAC reported spending approximately $42.7 million during the first two weeks of October, with $46.5 million in cash remaining as of October 14.The PAC has reported around $68.6 million in independent expenditures during the current midterm election cycle, primarily targeting competitive Senate races, according to FEC records compiled by the PaidForPolitics tracker.Texas senate race gets largest share of spendingThe largest share of the PAC's spending has gone towards the Texas Senate race. It has spent $27.9 million opposing Democratic candidate James Talarico and another $4.8 million supporting his Republican opponent, Ken Paxton. Forbes reported.America PAC has also spent approximately $9.3 million on the Ohio Senate race, followed by $7.7 million in Michigan, $2.7 million in Iowa and $2.1 million in Maine. The spending in these states has primarily focused on opposing Democratic candidates.Earlier this month, The New York Times reported that Musk had contributed more than $366 million to midterm election races by the end of September, including donations to America PAC and other outside groups.That figure included a $158 million donation to the Republican Senate Leadership Fund last month. The super PAC subsequently transferred an identical amount to the Texas PAC, which supports Paxton's campaign.Forbes estimated Musk's net worth at $909.8 billion as of late Thursday night, retaining his position as the world's richest person.You use AI every day. articles.title: In a 2010 Italian field study, researchers mixed solar-dried orange peel into steep soil plots; after 20 rain events, soil erosion was about 50% lower under the tested conditions
articles.summary: A 2010 study in Italy demonstrates that solar-dried orange peel can significantly decrease soil erosion on steep land, with findings showing a 50% reduction in erosion rates, highlighting its potential as a sustainable agricultural practice.
articles.body: Soil erosion can gradually strip away the fertile surface layer that plants depend on, especially on steep land exposed to heavy rainfall. Protection of slope areas has remained an issue to be solved by farmers and landowners. Several studies have been done to check whether agricultural residues, normally wasted after processing the food materials, can provide a solution to this problem. A 2010 study by Bombino and colleagues in southern Italy checked whether solar-dried citrus peel could help control runoff and soil erosion. The study results indicated that orange peel, which is normally left after producing juice, was effective in reducing soil erosion.Eight experimental plots tested the citrus-peel treatmentAccording to Bombino and colleagues’ 2010 paper on land spreading of solar-dried citrus peel, the experiment used eight plots, each measuring 2 square metres, arranged in two wooden boxes set at a 100% slope. In four plots, the researchers added citrus peel, while the remaining four were left untreated. The 100% slope indicates that the vertical rise is the same as the horizontal distance. Solar-dried citrus peel was shredded into small pieces (4 to 8 mm) and mixed into the top 3 cm of soil at a rate of 3 kg per square metre. Then, the plots were subjected to natural rainfall and the researchers were able to observe runoff and sediment loss in treated and untreated soils under field conditions. The experiment was conducted during 20 rain events. Different rainfall conditions and plots with different ground cover properties were observed.Soil erosion fell by about 50%According to Bombino and colleagues, the key result was a 50% reduction in soil erosion in the treated plots compared with the controls. There was a 10% average decrease in the surface runoff as well. During this experiment, sediment yield and sediment concentration were, on average, 55-60% less in treated plots than in the controls. The decrease in runoff varied depending on observations and reached up to 33% at maximum. Runoff is the water flowing over the soil surface, whereas sediment yield is the soil carried out of the plot. In other words, despite the small decrease in runoff volumes, the decrease in soil loss may be much higher. The results suggest that solar-dried citrus peel can help minimize erosion under the tested conditions. Yet, it does not mean that the same effect will take place under other conditions.Organic matter may have improved soil conditionsThe study authors hypothesized that adding citrus peel would improve soil quality and promote plant growth. Organic material affects soil structure and the passage of water and could thus aid in the passage of rainwater into the soil instead of running on top of it. Plants are able to act as a shield from raindrops and slow down surface water. Plant roots might also play a role in keeping soil particles bound together. Improved soil quality and plant development were two possible explanations offered for decreased erosion. This interpretation needs to be carefully qualified. While there were clear distinctions made between treated and untreated plots in the experiment, there was no way of proving the degree to which each potential mechanism contributed to the decreased erosion.Citrus waste also requires careful handlingUsing citrus peel on land could provide a useful outlet for waste from fruit-processing industries. However, applying organic waste to soil also requires consideration of what happens as it decomposes and releases liquid. A later study, Evaluating the Pollution Risk of Soil Due to Natural Drainage of Orange Peel: First Results, published in Environments in 2021, investigated the potential pollution risk associated with drainage from orange peel. In their study, the scientists studied the organic liquid that came out of the substance under the conditions of the experiment. The authors concluded that the risk of soil pollution from natural drainage of orange peel was negligible, given the limited amounts of leachate and organic load, although they noted that heavy rainfall could aggravate the hazard.The paper reports three lysimeter tests on orange peel: one with raw peel left to drain naturally and two others exposed to 100 mm of simulated rainfall after the peel had already drained or been solar-dried. In about 14 weeks, the peel volume fell by roughly 90% and the raw-peel test released 37.7 L of leachate, about 19% of the initial peel volume. The authors found that the organic load reaching the soil was negligible. Unlike the erosion study conducted in 2010, this study raises a new question. In combination, the studies show the need to consider both the advantages and disadvantages of using agricultural waste.Further field testing is neededThe 2010 study by Bombino and colleagues suggests that solar-dried citrus peel can reduce soil erosion, but only under the specific experimental conditions tested. This information could be useful in any attempt to preserve lands which are either steep or erosion-prone, as well as discovering other uses for by-products from agriculture. Nevertheless, the experiment was carried out on a relatively small number of plots under certain conditions in southern Italy. Further research is needed to test the treatment in different soil types and climates and to assess how long the effect lasts. For now, the study only suggests that citrus peel may be useful in soil conservation, not that it is a guaranteed solution. The actual applicability of the material will depend on its efficiency in real-life situations.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Watch: Two Philippine air force trainer aircraft collide mid-air; 4 pilots killed
articles.summary: Four pilots were killed after two Philippine air force trainer aircraft crashed during a training flight at an air base south of the capital Manila, the
articles.body: Four pilots were killed after two Philippine air force trainer aircraft crashed during a training flight at an air base south of the capital Manila, the military said on Saturday. A video of the incident showed that the planes collided mid-air.The accident occurred on Friday at Fernando Air Base in Batangas province and involved two SF-260 aircraft, the Philippine Air Force said in a statement.Both aircraft crashed within the grounds of the air base. No other casualties were reported, news agency Reuters reported.The air force has temporarily grounded its fleet of SF-260 trainer aircraft pending an investigation into the cause of the crash.The incident follows another fatal crash involving the same aircraft type in May, when two pilots were killed after an SF-260 went down in a mountainous area in the northern Philippines. In 2023, another SF-260 TP Marchetti crashed during a training flight, killing two pilots.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Will not sign': AISA chief Neha Bora defies Delhi police peace bond notice after HC setback
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: All India Students' Association president Neha Bora on Saturday said she would not sign a bond to \"keep peace\" before a special executive
articles.body: NEW DELHI: All India Students' Association president Neha Bora on Saturday said she would not sign a bond to "keep peace" before a special executive magistrate, a day after the Delhi high court dismissed her plea challenging the police notice directing her to furnish a Rs 10,000 bond with a surety."We don't have any conditions. We are not going to sign the bond," Bora said.Bora had moved the high court, arguing that the notice was vague, factually incorrect and unsupported by material establishing the likelihood of a breach of peace.She alleged that the proceedings were a "colourable exercise of preventive powers to suppress peaceful dissent, in violation of Articles 19(1)(a), 19(1)(b) and 21 of Constitution".During Thursday's hearing, Bora's counsel argued that citizens did not need permission to hoist the national flag, referring to the police notice alleging that she had hoisted it without valid permission.The notice, issued on October 17 under Section 126 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), directed Bora to appear before the magistrate on October 19 and explain why she should not execute a personal bond of Rs 10,000 with one surety "for keeping peace for a period of enquiry".Bora was taken into preventive detention on October 16 while on her way to participate in the Cockroach Janata Party's (CJP) 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march at Central Park in Connaught Place. She was released the following day.According to her petition, the police initiated proceedings over alleged sloganeering at Mandi House on October 16, repeated protests around Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS, and allegations that she had instigated people to join a demonstration at Connaught Place that day."The impugned notice rests on a prima facie incorrect fact, namely that the petitioner instigated people to participate in the demonstration at Central Park, CP on Oct 16. The petitioner's call and the incident alleged were different. The petitioner called for a peaceful gathering at Mandi House at 5.00 pm on Oct 16, and it is a matter of record that she was detained from Mandi House," Bora's petition stated.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Trump will take his dream to his grave': Iran determined to not allow US warships in Hormuz
articles.summary: Iran on Saturday vowed not to allow US military ships into the Persian Gulf “under any circumstances”, as tensions with Washington escalated amid threats
articles.body: Iran on Saturday vowed not to allow US military ships into the Persian Gulf “under any circumstances”, as tensions with Washington escalated amid threats of further military action by the United States.Iran's armed forces chief Ali Abdollahi remarked after US President Donald Trump threatened another "little Epic Fury" to force Iran's compliance, in case negotiations fail.“We will not allow US military ships in the Persian Gulf under any circumstances and at any time,” Iranian state television quoted the chief of staff of Iran’s armed forces, Ali Abdollahi, as saying. AFP reported.“The US president must dream of seeing the armed forces enter the Persian Gulf. He will take that dream to his grave,” Abdollahi added.Iranian forces have restricted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a key energy route connecting the Gulf to the wider world, since the war with the United States began on February 28. In response, Washington has imposed a counterblockade on Iranian ports and vessels.Tehran has required ships to obtain permission to transit the strait and has repeatedly targeted vessels attempting to pass through a southern route near the Omani coast.According to Iran’s Revolutionary Guards, several tankers attempting to use the route, which Tehran considers “illegal”, have been hit by mines in recent days.On Friday, the Guards said two supertankers carrying more than 4.5 million barrels of crude oil had been abandoned at sea after striking mines in the strategic waterway. AFP reported.Possible strike on Iran this weekend?The latest warning from Tehran came after US Ambassador to Turkiye Tom Barrack said on Friday that a US strike on Iran could take place over the weekend, while stressing that Trump remained open to a diplomatic agreement.“Could there be a strike this weekend? Absolutely,” Barrack said in an interview with Lebanese-Australian entrepreneur Mario Nawfal on Friday.Barrack, who also serves as Trump’s special envoy, said the US president remained willing to negotiate but warned that continued threats against the United States, its allies and Gulf countries would have consequences.“The president has been clear. I'm giving you American policy. President is very clear. He's open and available and accessible to a deal. And we've been at the table for months and months and months,” Barrack said.Hours later, Trump addressed a rally in Florida where he told Americans that the possibility of further military action was open.“We may do another little Epic Fury, or they'll agree,” Trump said.“If they're smart, they'll just say, 'Let's get down to business.' But, you know, I doubt they'll do that because perhaps they're not smart,” he added.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: When Sonia met Rajiv: Congress leader narrates her 1st meeting with husband in X debut
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi made her debut on social media platform X on Saturday, sharing a video in which she
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi made her debut on social media platform X on Saturday, sharing a video in which she recalled her first meeting with former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and offered a glimpse of her upcoming book, Belonging: A Journey of Love.The book, Sonia Gandhi's first, is scheduled to be launched on November 10. It recounts her personal journey, including her memories with Rajiv Gandhi and experiences from her younger days to the present.In the nearly two-minute video accompanying her first post on X, Sonia Gandhi recalled meeting Rajiv Gandhi at the Varsity Restaurant, a Greek eatery in Cambridge, England, where they were students.The video featured photographs of the couple and the restaurant where they first met."In a small Greek restaurant in Cambridge, my journey of love began. Rajiv and I created a world filled with love, laughter and memories. On 10th November, I share that world with you," she wrote in her post.Sonia Gandhi recalls meeting Rajiv Gandhi in CambridgeSpeaking in the video, the Congress MP recalled looking for Italian food while living in England, where she said the food available at the time did not suit her preferences."Food in England in those days was awful. In those days, you didn't have so many restaurants, you know, like you have today," she said.She explained that she was looking for a place serving food closer to what she was accustomed to, particularly Italian cuisine, when she discovered the Greek restaurant."And then, we discovered this place (Varsity Restaurant). It was a Greek restaurant where many European students, but also Indian students, used to go for their meals. And that is then where I met Rajiv in that very restaurant," she said.Recalling her first impression of Rajiv Gandhi, she said she felt almost immediately that he was someone she would want to spend her life with."When I first met him, I felt almost immediately that you know he was someone I would really love to be with. And, of course, I learned that it was the same for him," she said.Sonia Gandhi also recalled that a common friend introduced them. The two subsequently became friends and began attending parties with other students and visiting places together."I remember when I first met him, a friend, a common friend, introduced us. Then, you know, we became friends. Then going to parties with friends, or going to see sights, or… We went to a Valentine party where there were lots of students," she said.Describing what stood out to her about Rajiv Gandhi, she said his gentle nature had left a lasting impression."He was a very gentle-looking person. Of course, he was very good-looking. But that gentleness came through. So that was something which really touched me and struck me. So that, of course, I'll never forget when I first met him," she said.Sonia married Rajiv Gandhi on February 25, 1968.Upcoming memoir traces her personal journeyThe upcoming memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, explores Sonia Gandhi's life, from her childhood in post-war Italy and her romance with Rajiv Gandhi to her move to India and the personal losses that shaped her life and relationship with her adopted country.Her debut on X comes two days after she joined Instagram on Thursday and shared a video offering a first look at the book.In her first Instagram post, she expressed gratitude at being able to share the preview with readers and described the memoir as a story of love, duty, loss and finding a place to belong."I look forward to sharing it with you," she wrote in the post.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: In the 1950s, a Kentucky family bought 37 acres and later added a smaller access parcel; decades after the two were sold separately, new owners lost their court fight to use the neighbour's driveway
articles.summary: A property dispute in Kentucky has ended with a state appeals court ruling against a couple who claimed they had the right to use a neighbour’s pathway to
articles.body: A property dispute in Kentucky has ended with a state appeals court ruling against a couple who claimed they had the right to use a neighbour’s pathway to reach their land. The dispute centred on two adjoining parcels that once belonged to the same family: a roughly 37-acre property bought in the 1950s and a smaller, three-fourths-acre tract acquired about 20 years later. For years, the family used a pathway across the smaller parcel to reach parts of the larger property. But after the two tracts were sold separately, the new owners disagreed over whether that access could continue.On October 23, 2026, the Kentucky Court of Appeals upheld a jury’s decision that Charlie E. Stearns and Kathy Stearns had no legal easement allowing them to cross the adjoining property owned by John Warinner and Betty Warinner. As reported by American legal website Law Justia, the court found that evidence supported the jury’s conclusion that the Stearnses did not have a legal right to use the route.Two adjoining properties, sold separatelyAccording to Law Justia, John Warinner’s parents bought the larger tract, approximately 37 acres, in the 1950s. About two decades later, they purchased the adjoining smaller tract, measuring three-fourths of an acre. The parents used a pathway on the smaller parcel to reach portions of the larger property. However, John Warinner testified that his parents had also used alternative routes for about 20 years before buying the smaller tract.After his parents died, the two parcels were sold separately by a court-appointed Master Commissioner on the same day. The Stearnses purchased the larger tract, which adjoined land they already owned. The Warinners bought the smaller parcel. The Stearnses believed they were entitled to continue using the pathway across the smaller property. The Warinners disagreed and eventually put up barriers to prevent access.The disagreement led to a lawsuit in 2022. The Warinners accused the Stearnses of wrongly claiming an easement across their land and also brought a trespass claim against them. The case went to a jury trial in February 2025.Why the couple said they needed the pathwayThe Stearnses argued that their right to use the route had developed while both parcels were under common ownership. Their claim relied on the idea that a property owner’s long-standing use of one part of a property to benefit another part can, in some circumstances, create an easement when ownership is later divided. They argued that the route was an implied easement, including an easement by necessity and what they described as an “apparent easement”.There was evidence supporting their position. Two of John Warinner’s sisters testified that the rough terrain made it extremely difficult, if not practically impossible, to reach the larger tract without crossing the smaller one. But other witnesses gave a different account. John Warinner said alternative access routes existed, and a surveyor testified that the Stearnses could reach the larger property without crossing the Warinners’ land.Warinner also identified an older road that could be used after repairs, although he acknowledged that it needed work before it would be usable. The appeals court said the evidence gave the jury a factual question to decide: whether crossing the smaller tract was reasonably necessary for access to the larger one.What the court said about an easement by necessityUnder Kentucky law, an easement by necessity generally requires common ownership before the properties were divided, a subsequent separation of ownership and a strict need to use the neighbouring property to obtain access. The appeals court said an easement by necessity generally cannot be established if the landowner has another way to reach a public road, even if that alternative is inconvenient.Because Warinner and the surveyor testified that other access was available, the court found there was enough evidence to support the jury’s rejection of the claim. The court also considered the argument that the pathway qualified as a ‘quasi-easement.’ This legal concept can arise when an owner uses one part of a property to benefit another and the use is sufficiently established, apparent and reasonably necessary to the land.The judges said the Stearnses had to show more than a history of using the pathway. They needed to establish that the route was reasonably necessary to the enjoyment of the larger tract. Evidence of alternative access meant the jury could reasonably find that this requirement had not been met.Kentucky does not recognise a separate “apparent easement” theoryThe Stearnses also argued that the pathway qualified as an apparent easement, a separate category they said could justify their access. According to Law Justia, the Court of Appeals rejected that argument. The judges also rejected the couple’s suggestion that the jury’s brief deliberations indicated that it had ignored evidence or committed misconduct. They said there was no concrete evidence of improper conduct. The jury had found that the Stearnses trespassed, but awarded the Warinners no damages on that claim.The appeals court concluded that the evidence supported the jury’s verdict and affirmed the lower court’s judgment. The opinion was marked “not to be published”. The ruling leaves the Stearnses without the claimed legal right to use the pathway across the Warinners’ smaller parcel. It also underlines a key point in property disputes: a route used for years does not automatically become a legally enforceable easement when neighbouring properties are sold separately.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Tumhare chehre aa gaye hain, nikal jao waha se': How handlers used news coverage to guide shooters after Tiger Shroff firing
articles.summary: MUMBAI: News coverage of the investigation into the firing at actor Tiger Shroff allegedly became a real-time alert system for the three shooters as they
articles.body: MUMBAI: News coverage of the investigation into the firing at actor Tiger Shroff allegedly became a real-time alert system for the three shooters as they fled Mumbai, with their handlers relaying updates through encrypted messaging applications and instructing them to change routes when their identities were exposed, police sources said on Saturday.The three accused were apprehended aboard a train in Kota on October 19, a day after the shooting in Mumbai’s Juhu area.Investigators believe that continuous updates about the police probe and the suspects’ movements prompted the trio to switch between modes of transport in an attempt to evade arrest.How handlers used news reports to guide the suspectsAccording to sources in the crime branch investigating the case, the handlers were monitoring television coverage and passing information directly to the shooters through encrypted Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) messaging applications.At one point during the escape, when news channels aired visuals of the attack, one of the main suspects allegedly received an urgent instruction on his mobile phone: “Tumhare chehre aa gaye hain, nikal jao waha se” (Your faces are out, get out of there).The actor escaped relatively unhurt on the evening of October 18 after two shooters fired multiple rounds at his car in Mumbai’s Juhu area.The incident triggered a multi-state investigation, leading to the arrest of 10 people from Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Haryana. Shroff’s driver and a vlogger sustained injuries in the firing.Signal, Zangi under scannerThe three key accused have been identified as Phool Singh (18), Rehan Rahisuddin Ansari (18) and Rithik Mahto (22). They were intercepted and arrested by Kota Police in Rajasthan on October 19 and are currently in police custody until October 31.Analysis of digital evidence indicated that Rehan was in constant contact with others through VoIP-based applications, crime branch sources said.Applications such as Signal and Zangi can be used for internet-based communication without requiring a mobile number for registration, they added.Police sources said reports about the recovery of the attackers’ motorcycle in Andheri and their subsequent train journey were also relayed to the shooters by their handlers.Shooters allegedly switched transport modesAccording to crime branch sources, the steady stream of updates prompted the trio to repeatedly change their mode of transport as they tried to escape.“This constant feed prompted the trio to frequently shift modes of transport, moving from a motorcycle to a train, followed by a cab, before planning to board a bus from Surat.“The delay at the Surat bus terminal eventually led them to board another train, where they were apprehended by the Kota police following a prompt alert from the Mumbai Police,” they said.The Crime Branch is questioning the accused in custody to establish how the firearms were procured and identify those involved in supplying weapons and providing logistical support.Mumbai Police have named gangster Anil Pandit as a wanted accused in the case. Pandit, an alleged associate of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang believed to be operating from the US, had claimed responsibility for the October 18 attack on Shroff in a social media post.The investigation is continuing, with police seeking to establish the roles of all those allegedly involved in planning and executing the firing, as well as those who provided weapons and logistical assistance.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Mystery surrounds death of Class 12 student found burnt behind Delhi school guard room
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: An 18-year-old Class 12 student was found in a burnt condition behind a school’s guard room in Delhi’s Krishna Nagar on Saturday.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: An 18-year-old Class 12 student was found in a burnt condition behind a school’s guard room in Delhi’s Krishna Nagar on Saturday.Delhi Police said they received a PCR call about a fire at the school. Personnel from Krishna Nagar police station reached the spot and found the student in a burnt condition.During preliminary proceedings, police recovered certain materials from the scene and the student’s school bag. The crime team was called to inspect the spot and collect evidence.The girl’s elder sister told reporters that she had accompanied her to school to drop her off, along with her niece. She said the girl appeared happy and walked into the school smiling.“She was laughing when she went inside. I don’t know what happened after that,” the sister said.She added that she received a call from the school around 12.40pm informing her that something serious had happened. The sister broke down while recounting the incident.Fire officer Anoop Singh said the cause of the fire had not yet been established and that one fire tender had been sent to the school.“We received a call that a child had set a fire inside a school. Upon arriving at the scene and entering the school, we found a child who had been burned, lying behind a water tank. We don’t know her exact age, but she was in the 12th grade. Only one vehicle from our team arrived. It is not yet clear what was used to start the fire. She was taken away by an ambulance; the hospital will be able to provide details on what happened,” he said.BJP MLA Anil Goyal described the incident as unfortunate and said the police and local administration were investigating the circumstances surrounding the student’s death.“This is a major, unfortunate incident. The reasons behind her suicide are a matter for investigation. Our police, the local administration, and officials from the SDM’s office are all looking into it. The body has now been sent for a post-mortem...” he said.A fire official who reached the spot said they received information around 11.58am that a student had allegedly set herself on fire inside the school. “When we entered the school, we found the student in a burnt condition behind a water tank on the left side. Her face was completely burnt,” he said.Delhi Police said further enquiry was underway as investigators examined the circumstances leading to the incident.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: A creator in the UAE fitted 150 words onto one sticky note, and her unusual writing feat went viral
articles.summary: A small sticky note has helped Pushpajothi Ravikumar turn a childhood ambition into a Guinness World Records achievement.
articles.body: A small sticky note has helped Pushpajothi Ravikumar turn a childhood ambition into a Guinness World Records achievement. The 29-year-old, who works as a senior cloud engineer in the United Arab Emirates, managed to write 150 different words on a single sticky note, setting a record for the most words written on the small piece of paper. Her attempt, completed in Dubai, attracted widespread attention after she shared a video of the feat. The response reached far beyond her immediate circle, drawing interest from viewers, colleagues and family members.How did the UAE creator fit 150 words on one sticky noteAccording to Guinness World Records, Pushpajothi Ravikumar, known as Jothi, achieved the record by carefully selecting words and making efficient use of the limited writing space. Rather than trying to fill the note with long expressions, she chose simple, short words, most of which contained just three letters.The approach allowed her to include more words without making the writing completely unreadable. Although fitting as many words as possible was central to the challenge, legibility remained an important consideration. Jothi explained to Guinness World Records that she had to establish a limit because the words still needed to be read.The record was not simply a matter of filling every available gap with ink. It required her to balance the number of words against the space available, ensuring that the finished note could still be understood.On 19 August 2026, Guinness World Records identified Jothi as the record holder for writing 150 different words on one sticky note. The achievement took place in Dubai and marked a significant personal milestone for the UAE-based engineer.What inspired Jothi to attempt the unusual writing challengeJothi's interest in record-breaking began long before she decided to attempt the sticky-note challenge. In her interview with Guinness World Records, she explained that she had watched the organisation's records since childhood and dreamed of becoming part of its collection of record holders.Seeing other people achieve unique feats inspired her, although she did not initially know which achievement might eventually become her own. The idea of writing an extraordinary number of words on a tiny piece of paper eventually came to her, prompting her to apply for the record attempt.The official Guinness World Records report also noted that Jothi enjoys experimenting with different handwriting styles. That interest gave her a natural starting point for a challenge that depended on how efficiently she could use a limited area of paper.Despite the unusual nature of the task, she did not need several attempts to secure the title. According to Guinness World Records, she broke the record on her first attempt, making the result particularly rewarding.The sticky-note world record attracted massive online attentionThe achievement gained another dimension when Jothi shared a video of her attempt on Instagram. What began as a personal milestone soon reached a much wider audience, with the video attracting nearly one million views.The attention extended to people who knew her personally, including family members, friends and colleagues, who began asking her about the accomplishment.The simple materials helped make the feat easy to understand. Viewers did not need specialist equipment to appreciate the difficulty of fitting 150 distinct words into such a small space. The contrast between the size of the note and the number of words written on it gave the attempt its appeal.What does the achievement mean for Jothi's future plansFor Jothi, the record has provided both recognition and a boost in confidence. Speaking to Guinness World Records, she described the platform as a way for people to display talents they might not have realised they possessed. She also expressed the belief that everyone has something unique within them.Although the feat might appear modest compared with records involving extraordinary physical or technical challenges, it carried considerable meaning for someone who had wanted to join the record books since childhood.The response to her attempt also encouraged her to consider further challenges. According to the Guinness World Records report, she is keen to break more records in the future. Her next achievement has not been specified in the reports, but the sticky-note record has given her a starting point.Sticky notes are commonly used for reminders and brief messages, but Jothi's attempt pushed the limits of what could be written on one while keeping the words readable. The method depended on choosing short words and making careful use of the available surface without relying on elaborate equipment.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 2006, a New York couple lost their nine-day-old daughter in an emergency room; 20 years later, their foundation says it has trained 6,500 physicians, and a joint charity gala has raised nearly $2 million
articles.summary: In July 2006, Phyllis and Andrew Rabinowitz took their newborn daughter, Rebecca, to doctors and an emergency department because she was congested,
articles.body: In July 2006, Phyllis and Andrew Rabinowitz took their newborn daughter, Rebecca, to doctors and an emergency department because she was congested, feeding slowly and having difficulty breathing. Her symptoms were repeatedly diagnosed as a common cold, according to the family’s account published by the R Baby Foundation. Rebecca died on July 21, nine days after her birth. The couple later learned that their daughter had contracted an enteroviral infection, which can be life-threatening in newborns. Her death led them to establish the R Baby Foundation, with the aim of improving emergency medical care for babies and children.Twenty years later, the organisation says it has raised $18 million and trained more than 6,500 physicians across over 1,000 hospitals. On October 21, 2026, it marked the anniversary with a joint fundraising gala in New York City alongside the COPE Foundation, which supports families coping with the death of a loved one. According to the official website of R Baby Foundation, the event raised nearly $2 million. The money will support paediatric emergency-care preparedness and grief-support services for bereaved families.How Rebecca’s death led to the foundationRebecca was born four weeks prematurely on July 13, 2006, according to R Baby Foundation’s website. She spent five days in a neonatal intensive care unit before being discharged. The next day, her parents noticed severe congestion, thick mucus, slow feeding and breathing difficulties. They sought medical attention, including at a hospital emergency department, but Rebecca was sent home after her symptoms were assessed as a common cold, the family said.She died on the morning of July 21. The family later learned that the illness was an enteroviral infection. The Rabinowitzes established R Baby Foundation in 2006 to address gaps in the training, equipment and procedures used to treat babies and children in emergency settings. The organisation funds medical education, research, training and equipment, working with children's hospitals to help improve care in community hospitals, where many children receive emergency treatment.What the foundation says it has achieved in 20 yearsR Baby Foundation says it has raised more than $18 million and trained over 6,500 physicians across more than 1,000 hospitals since its establishment. It also says its work reaches more than one million children annually through partnerships with medical institutions, including Yale, Columbia, Johns Hopkins and Mount Sinai. The organisation has established INSPIRE, which it describes as the world's largest paediatric simulation-based research network. Its programmes focus on helping medical professionals recognise and respond to emergencies involving babies and children. The foundation is also pushing for wider policy changes.According to its website, its advocacy has contributed to paediatric emergency-readiness legislation in Texas, Florida and Utah. It is supporting the proposed Babies’ and Children’s Emergency Care Act, known as BECA, which aims to strengthen emergency-care preparedness nationally. R Baby Foundation says about 2,100 children die each year in emergency departments that are not adequately prepared to treat them. It also cites estimates that 83% of US emergency departments lack the equipment, training or protocols needed for paediatric emergencies, despite approximately 30 million paediatric emergency-room visits annually.Why another foundation joined the galaThe event also supported COPE Foundation, short for Connecting Our Paths Eternally, which works with parents, siblings and families grieving the loss of a loved one. COPE was founded by Lillian Julien after her 20-year-old daughter, Michelle, died in a car accident in 1992. In her founder’s statement on COPE’s website, Julien describes how the loss inspired her to create a support network for grieving families.COPE now offers professionally facilitated support groups, workshops, retreats, educational resources and bereavement camps. Its programmes are intended to help parents and children cope with grief alongside people who have experienced similar losses. According to the gala announcement, COPE served more than 1,100 families and individuals in 2025.The two organisations approach loss from different directions. R Baby Foundation works to improve emergency care in the hope of preventing avoidable tragedies, while COPE supports people living with the aftermath of a death.Nearly $2 million raised at New York galaThe October 21 event, called Cirquetacular, brought around 500 supporters, physicians, advocates and families to Capitale in New York City. It marked 20 years of R Baby Foundation’s work and raised nearly $2 million for the two organisations, according to the announcement. The evening included dinner, a live auction, an aerial performance and a fundraising appeal. CC Capital and law firm Skadden were the presenting sponsors, and singer Jac Ross performed at the close of the event.For the Rabinowitzes, the anniversary marked two decades of work that began after Rebecca’s death. The foundation’s stated goal remains to make emergency departments across the United States better prepared to care for children, while its partnership with COPE also directs support towards families who have lost someone they love.You use AI every day. articles.title: Michael and Susan Dell's foundation backs free skills training in Texas; a 2026 update reports that 78% of Skillpoint Alliance graduates find jobs and average monthly earnings reach $3,600
articles.summary: The philanthropic organisation founded by Michael Dell and Susan Dell has spotlighted the growing impact of free skilled-trades training in Texas,
articles.body: The philanthropic organisation founded by Michael Dell and Susan Dell has spotlighted the growing impact of free skilled-trades training in Texas, reporting that a large majority of participants secure employment shortly after completing the programme. According to a 2026 update from the Michael & Susan Dell Foundation, 78% of graduates from Skillpoint Alliance find jobs after completing their training, while graduates earn an average of $3,600 per month and increase their earnings by an average of 150%.How the training worksSkillpoint’s pitch is speed and a direct link to employers. Traditional training programmes, the foundation notes, often take months or years, cost thousands of dollars and may not lead to available jobs. Skillpoint instead builds its free five-week courses with employers who are hiring now, so participants train for open positions companies need to fill today.Participants earn industry-recognised certifications, visit job sites and train on electrical systems, HVAC equipment and plumbing installations designed to mirror real working conditions. They also receive mentoring and help with job placement.Industry certifications and job placement supportParticipants in the programme receive hands-on training, earn industry-recognised certifications, visit job sites and receive mentoring and job placement assistance. According to the organisation, employer partnerships shape every aspect of the curriculum, creating a more direct pathway from training to employment. The results have been significant. The foundation reports that more than three-quarters of graduates secure jobs after completing the programme, while many move into careers that offer greater stability, higher wages and long-term advancement opportunities.Addressing Texas' skilled worker shortageThe programme comes as Texas continues to face growing demand for skilled workers across critical industries. According to the foundation, many employers struggle to fill essential roles, while adults seeking career advancement often face barriers such as lengthy training periods and high educational costs.The organisation highlighted the story of a graduate named Mariah, who transitioned from security work into an HVAC technician role after completing five weeks of training. She now works as a start-up technician, inspecting and testing newly installed HVAC systems before they reach customers.Expansion planned across Central TexasTo meet growing demand, Skillpoint Alliance is expanding its operations in South Austin and New Braunfels. The organisation is further planning to increase the training capacity by updating the families, hiring more instructors and support staff and also running multiple cohorts. The Michael & Susan Dell Foundation claimed that the expansion is aimed at helping more Texans gain access to fast, employer-connected training programmes that can lead to stable careers and improved economic mobility while helping businesses fill critical workforce gaps.You use AI every day. articles.title: Ukraine says Starlink, Starshield connections return to normal speeds after weeklong disruption
articles.summary: Ukraine's Starlink and Starshield satellite communications systems are operating at speeds exceeding 400 km/h, the country's defence minister said on
articles.body: Ukraine's Starlink and Starshield satellite communications systems are operating at speeds exceeding 400 km/h, the country's defence minister said on Saturday, after more than a week of service disruptions that hit military operations.“The ministry of defence's monitoring systems are recording a return to normal speed for Starlink/Starshield. We are recording a speed of over 400 kph. The connection is stable,” defence minister Evhenii Khmara told reporters.Ukraine relies on SpaceX's civilian Starlink satellite network and its military-grade Starshield system to support military communications and operations, including efforts to defend against Russian missile and drone attacks.The Ukrainian defence ministry said its monitoring systems had previously recorded disruptions to the services, but that speed metrics had now returned to normal. However, it did not confirm whether service had been fully restored, Reuters reported.Khmara also highlighted the importance of the recovery for military operations.“This result is above all important for our front, for our soldiers, for the operation of drones, for logistics and for communications,” he said, according to AFP.The restrictions, first reported on October 14, affected Ukraine's ability to intercept Russian attack drones and disrupted communications along the front line, Ukrainian officials said, according to Reuters. Sources told the news agency that connection speeds had fallen to around 160 km/h or lower.The satellite network has become a point of tension between Kyiv and Washington. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had previously accused the United States of helping Russia by failing to warn Kyiv about incoming missile strikes and weakening Ukraine's military response by throttling Starlink speeds, AFP reported.Khmara credited Zelenskyy's “firm stance” on the issue, saying it was “bearing fruit”, AFP reported.The disruption followed US President Donald Trump's announcement of a deal to buy Russian diesel and his decision to waive new sanctions on Moscow, while pressing Ukraine to stop striking Russian oil refineries, Reuters reported.On Friday, Trump said that if problems with access to Starlink communications systems in Ukraine persisted, he would “get it straightened out”.You use AI every day. articles.title: In a first, forest staff from 6 states to get Israeli Krav Maga training to tackle forest crimes
articles.summary: Uttarakhand Forestry Training Academy to train 170 forest staff from 6 states and J&K in Israeli Krav Maga from Nov to tackle forest crimes and attacks.
articles.body: Dehradun: In a first for India’s frontline forest personnel, Uttarakhand Forestry Training Academy (UFTA) in Haldwani will introduce Krav Maga, an Israeli self-defence technique, into its training curriculum from Nov to help staff tackle attacks by timber and sand mafias, poachers and forest encroachers. Around 170 foresters and forest rangers from six states and Jammu & Kashmir will undergo training in the unarmed combat system, which focuses on responding to real-life threats, including assaults involving weapons and multiple attackers. The academy introduced the initiative after an internal assessment found that around 60 frontline forest personnel had lost their lives in the line of duty in Uttarakhand.UFTA director Sanjiv Chaturvedi said the two-month programme would cover around 130 foresters from Uttarakhand and Punjab, currently undergoing training at the academy, and 40 forest rangers from Jammu & Kashmir, Meghalaya, Mizoram and Madhya Pradesh. “The training will commence for two months starting November,” he said. Certified Krav Maga instructors, who have previously trained police and customs personnel at National Police Academy in Hyderabad and in Mumbai, will conduct the sessions. Officials said only five to six certified instructors of the technique were currently available in India.The academy, which has trained frontline forest personnel since 1979, decided to introduce Krav Maga after examining fatalities involving staff confronting timber and sand mafias, encroachers and other offenders. Its assessment documented particularly violent incidents, including one in which a forest official was burnt alive and another in which an official’s body parts were severed. Officials said such attacks highlighted the need to equip field personnel with practical defensive skills alongside conventional enforcement training. The technique had previously been taught to police and customs personnel and probationary IAS officers.The first phase, beginning in Nov, will involve two weeks of intensive practice in defending against single and multiple attackers, including those carrying sticks, axes, knives, sharp-edged weapons and firearms. The second phase, scheduled for Dec, will focus on defensive manoeuvres in dense forests, on uneven ground and in poor visibility. Trainees will also practise techniques to escape when surrounded and to disarm assailants while minimising the risk of injury.Academy officials said the programme aimed to reduce casualties during enforcement operations and improve personnel’s ability to respond swiftly to threats from organised forest crime. UFTA will meet the initial expenditure from funds allocated for training at state forest training academies.Stay updated with the latest Dehradun news. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Aries, Weekly Horoscope, October 25 to October 31, 2026: Charm brings success, but patience keeps you grounded
articles.summary: General: The week opens on a bright note, Aries, and you’ll feel it almost at once. Early in the week, your presence carries weight.
articles.body: General:The week opens on a bright note, Aries, and you’ll feel it almost at once. Early in the week, your presence carries weight. People listen when you speak, and even casual conversations can turn in your favour. There is a social warmth around you, like a clear morning after sticky weather. Family cheer also lifts your mood, and some of you may attend a gathering, small celebration, or community event that reminds you how much goodwill you’ve built over time. You’ll notice that your words have extra charm now. Use that gift gently, because one kind sentence can smooth an old wrinkle.Still, this isn’t a week for acting only on impulse. Beneath the applause and easy wins, there is a thread of confusion. You may second guess yourself even after making the right call. Strange, isn’t it? Outward respect, inward wobble. By the middle of the week, courage rises and you may feel tempted to take on an unusual task, make a sudden trip, or chase an idea simply because it excites you. Do it with open eyes. Delay any big purchase linked with travel or machinery. The second half asks for patience, hard work, and a steady hand. Restlessness may creep in, especially if your schedule fills up with errands, family obligations, or unfinished tasks.As the weekend approaches, your world becomes more local and personal. Neighbours, siblings, old friends, and familiar faces matter more than grand plans. A new friendship may begin in a simple setting, perhaps over tea, a family visit, or a nearby celebration. At the same time, don’t scatter your energy. Keep your feet on the ground, your meals simple, and your driving careful. This week rewards the Aries who can balance fire with common sense.Love and Relationships:Your emotional weather changes more than once this week. In the first part, family ties feel warmer and more cooperative. A spouse or partner may step in helpfully with domestic matters, and relatives seem more willing to support your plans. If you are single, you’re likely to attract people through conversation rather than drama. Your voice carries softness early in the week, and that can win hearts faster than any grand display. A family event or social visit may also bring a pleasant introduction. Nothing too filmi, but enough to make you smile on the way home.Midweek needs care. There is a clear sign of friction with a spouse or partner, mostly because both sides want to be heard first. Hot words come quickly for you now. Once spoken, they hang in the room like smoke. If a small disagreement starts over routine matters, travel, spending, timing, or who forgot what, don’t keep feeding it. Step back. Drink water. Come back later. The good news is that this tension doesn’t define the whole week. It passes if you refuse to turn every irritation into a battle.Toward the weekend, relationships settle into a more ordinary rhythm. Not dramatic, not cold, simply manageable. That’s not a bad thing. Married natives may find comfort in practical teamwork, especially around the house or while dealing with relatives. Children bring encouraging news or make you proud through effort and results. An old friend may reappear, and with that meeting comes a reminder of who has stood by you through different seasons. Hold on to those bonds. They are quieter than passion, but often much stronger.Education and Career:This week begins with promise in both career and studies. If you run a business, orders, enquiries, or client interest can increase early on, and not always from expected places. Doors open through reputation, referrals, and word of mouth. People trust your capability. That matters. Those in service or office roles may also find that seniors notice their reliability. If there’s a presentation, meeting, public dealing, or negotiation in the first half, go in prepared. You’re likely to leave a better impression than you realise.Students also have a supportive current this week. The mind is especially receptive in the early and later parts of the week, so this is a good time to revise, clear pending work, and ask teachers the questions you’ve been postponing. Midweek, your courage grows, but concentration may become patchy. You’ll want to attempt something difficult, perhaps a competitive topic, a new project, or a demanding subject. Good. Just don’t skip the basics. A bold mind still needs a timetable. Keep your study desk clean and your phone away for fixed hours. Simple discipline will help more than bursts of motivation.By Thursday onward, hard work becomes the real story. Results don’t come free. You may feel tense, lazy one moment and determined the next. That back and forth can be tiring. Yet a brave decision taken now can shape the next few weeks well, especially if it concerns workload, deadlines, or a practical change in routine. Support from a younger sibling or someone junior may unexpectedly strengthen your confidence. Keep going, even if progress looks slow. This week respects effort more than speed.Money and Finance:Money matters begin on a hopeful note. You may receive income from different sources, and there is a sense of financial satisfaction early in the week. If you are in business, fresh orders can improve your cash flow. If you are employed, side earnings, delayed payments, or family support may lighten your mind. There is also a favourable breeze for speculation, but only if you think before moving. Don’t bet on excitement. Don’t follow noise. You may hear many opinions around you, and strangely, this is one week when your own confidence may wobble even while luck is supporting you.Midweek and later, the tone changes. Financial progress continues, but it becomes clearly linked to hard work. Money won’t fall into your lap. It will come because you chased a payment, finished a task, accepted extra work, or stayed disciplined when others became lazy. That’s the real lesson here. Also, postpone a vehicle purchase for now. The timing is not clean, and there may be hidden stress around maintenance, paperwork, or sudden expense. Better to wait than regret.The weekend brings social spending temptations, especially if there is a neighbourly function or informal get together. Keep your wallet closed if the spending is only for show. You do not need to prove your generosity every time someone calls. Food outside should also be limited, partly for health and partly because small casual expenses can pile up this week. Save where you can. Spend where it counts. That simple line will protect you.Health and Well-being:Your energy is uneven this week, Aries. Early on, the spirit feels bright, but the body sends smaller warnings. The right eye may trouble some of you, especially from screen strain, lack of sleep, or too much time in bright light. Don’t ignore it. Midweek is more delicate. You may feel daring and physically capable, yet this is exactly when overexertion, rushing, or careless travel can tire you out. Short journeys need planning. If you are driving, stay alert. If you are riding with someone else, avoid last minute chaos and leave on time.Stress builds quietly from Thursday onward. Hard work, mental agitation, and unfinished responsibilities can make you restless. Then comes laziness, not because you are weak, but because the body wants recovery. Listen to that signal. Sleep on time. Eat warm, simple food. Skip outside snacks for a few days, especially over the weekend, because digestion looks sensitive. If you’ve been promising yourself a healthier routine, this is the week to start with very small things. A morning walk. Less caffeine. More water. Nothing fancy.Emotionally too, you’ll need cooling methods. Arguments with a spouse or pressure from work can sit in your chest longer than you admit. Don’t carry every irritation like a badge. Speak less when angry. Breathe before replying. Meet an old friend if the chance comes, because familiar company can ground you beautifully now. By the weekend, the best medicine is simplicity, home food, careful travel, and enough rest to calm your racing mind.Get the latest astrology news and horoscope updates. articles.title: Omar Abdullah to MLAs: Stop sending WhatsApp messages, knocking on my and Farooq’s doors for ministerial berths; opposition calls it ‘cult of self’
articles.summary: SRINAGAR: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah, after meeting Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha on Saturday, said a cabinet expansion was on the
articles.body: SRINAGAR: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah, after meeting Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha on Saturday, said a cabinet expansion was on the cards and urged party colleagues to stop sending him lengthy WhatsApp messages and book-length profiles seeking ministerial berths.He also advised them against knocking on his door or that of his father and National Conference president, Dr Farooq Abdullah, to lobby for ministerial positions. The opposition described Omar’s portrayal of his party MLAs as demeaning to the political class and called it “the cult of self”.“The lieutenant governor sahab returned to Srinagar. In the meantime, his health had not been good, so I wanted to inquire about his well-being. There are also several issues on which it was necessary to meet him and seek his opinion from time to time. It had been a long time since I met him, so I sought an appointment today. He gave me time,” Omar told reporters after meeting the LG.“I know you people are not interested in anything else. You want to know whether I discussed the cabinet reshuffle with the LG sahab. Yes, absolutely. I sought an appointment with him for the expansion (of cabinet) and requested him to fix a time in the first two or three days of next week. So that I will make some changes and expand my council of ministers,” Omar said.He said the LG would fix a time for the process.“Now that I have told you about the reshuffle, I want to make a request to my colleagues, as news might have already spread about next week’s reshuffle. There is no need to knock on Farooq Abdullah’s door, my door or anyone else’s door,” Omar said.“The decision about who will become a minister has been taken. I request my colleagues to be patient. What is destined for them will happen. First, it is in God’s hands and then we took the decision. Whoever is destined to become a minister will become one. But please, do not knock on doors now. Do not send me WhatsApp messages,” he said.“I am receiving so many WhatsApp messages, with people writing lengthy resumes and sending me entire books. It is as if I do not know these people. They are sending me their complete biodata, as though I am not already familiar with them,” he said.“So please, do not send WhatsApp messages, call or knock on doors. Whatever has to happen will happen in the next two or three days,” Omar said.Omar was sworn in on Oct 16, 2024, along with five ministers, including deputy CM Surinder Choudhary. At present, three cabinet berths remain vacant. Under the norms, the strength of the council of ministers cannot exceed 10% of the total strength of the assembly. The J&K assembly has 90 members, capping the council of ministers at nine.Omar has allocated deputy CM Surinder Kumar Choudhary the portfolios of public works, industries and commerce, mining, labour and skill development. Sakeena Itoo handles health and medical education, school education, higher education and social welfare. Javed Ahmed Rana oversees water resources, forests, environment and tribal affairs. Javid Ahmad Dar is tasked with agriculture, panchayati raj and cooperatives. Satish Sharma is responsible for food, consumer affairs, transport, science and IT, youth affairs, sports and training.Leader of Opposition and BJP's Sunil Sharma, who has been claiming that the NC will "implode" if Omar goes ahead with the cabinet expansion, said, “The CM is behaving like a king. Like a king, he doesn’t like people visiting his home. He wants only a close coterie around him, with everyone else reduced to reporting to them. He is out to demean his own MLAs and has repeatedly humiliated them inside and outside the Assembly,” he added.Peoples Conference chairman Sajad Lone sharply reacted to Omar’s statement, calling it “the cult of self”.“I watched CM sahib talking to the media after meeting LG sahib. What a contemptuous and disdainful way of asking his party MLAs to not pester him for a ministerial berth. I honestly can’t believe that these MLAs are comfortable with such belittling and humiliating remarks,” Lone said.“If you are unable to accommodate them in the cabinet, you can spare them from public humiliation,” he added.“Anyway, these are internal party matters and I should not have commented. But there is always a spillover. You may direct the derision at your own members, but it invariably belittles the political class. I wonder how these elected members face their electors when they know they are treated like unworthy and incapable schoolboys,” Lone added.Stay updated with the latest Srinagar news.
